predecessors.name: Iberian Union
predecessors.text: the Principality of Catalonia with Roussillon: the provinces of Barcelona, Gerona, Lerida and most of Tarragona, and the north now in the Pyrénées-Orientales

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: Catalonia under the protection of Louis XIII, recognised as Count of Barcelona

rulers.name: Louis XIII of France (as Count of Barcelona, Louis I)
rulers.title: Count of Barcelona

ledger.x: 1640: Barcelona rises in the Bloody Corpus and the Principality of Catalonia is in revolt against Philip IV.
1640: the Reapers' War begins between the Principality and the Spanish Crown.
17 January 1641: the Catalan Republic is proclaimed under French protection.

January 1641 (closing the pair, confidence 1): the independent Catalan state ends, but the war with Spain goes on under French protection; the page has Spain capture Barcelona only in 1652 ('the French authorities renounced Catalonia, but held control of Roussillon').

wars.name: Franco-Spanish War (1635-1659)
wars.outcome: Stalemate 1637-1659; the Treaty of the Pyrenees (5 or 7 November 1659, the page gives both) gives France Artois, Hainaut towns and Roussillon; Louis XIV 'renounced his claim to be Count of Barcelona and King of Catalonia'.

certainty.note: The Principality's frontier with Aragon and the Tortosa end of Tarragona province are Cliopatria approximations; the Pyrenean frontier with France is the Roussillon-Cerdanya line the Treaty of the Pyrenees only moved in 1659.
